summary:
GravityWare is an AI assisted astronaut health monitoring prototype developed by Team BigwIN for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It provides individual astronaut accounts, daily health logging, personal health history, interactive trend visualisation, and downloadable PDF and CSV reports. Its experimental early warning feature screens for unusual patterns, while its gravity aware assessment and education pages explore health monitoring considerations across orbital microgravity, the Moon (0.16g), and Mars (0.38g).

GravityWare also demonstrates a human in the loop collaboration workflow: an astronaut requests a review, a doctor records an assessment, and Mission Control documents an operational decision. The astronaut can then view the review outcome.

The prototype uses synthetic demonstration records and is not connected to live astronaut telemetry or NASA systems. Its AI screening and gravity comparisons are experimental, not clinically validated, and do not diagnose or prescribe treatment. GravityWare aims to support organised health tracking and informed communication during long duration space missions.

"GravityWare " Understanding Health Beyond Earth

Team BigwIN | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

USER Manual (Open and Read before test the system)

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bMpgNhks8c57x621Hw6P58LrpQqsrhgQ/view?usp=drive_link

What it does

GravityWare is a Streamlit web application prototype for astronaut health monitoring during long duration space missions. It brings daily health logging, personal history, trend visualisation, gravity environment education, experimental pattern screening, and a demonstration medical review workflow into one platform.

How it works

  • Astronaut accounts: Individual sign in and profile based access.
  • Daily health records: Log indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, body temperature, sleep, stress, and fatigue.
  • Health history and reports: Review saved records and export PDF or CSV reports.
  • Experimental early-warning screening: Explore unusual patterns in personal health records. This is an experimental screening feature, not a validated medical prediction system.
  • Gravity-aware assessment: Compare an astronaut's personal history with their saved mission environment and explore orbital microgravity, lunar gravity (0.16g), and Martian gravity (0.38g).
  • Education: Explore human spaceflight health considerations in the context of NASA Human Research Program resources.
  • Human-in-the-loop collaboration: An astronaut can request a review; a doctor can record an assessment and recommendations; Mission Control can document an operational decision; and the astronaut can view the recorded outcome.

Benefits and intended impact

GravityWare demonstrates how health records, personal trends, educational context, and human review could be organised in one interface. It aims to encourage consistent self monitoring and clearer communication between astronauts, medical reviewers, and mission operations teams.

Technology

  • Python and Streamlit
  • Supabase Authentication and PostgreSQL
  • Pandas and Plotly
  • ReportLab for PDF reports
  • GitHub for source code hosting

ChatGPT was used for ideation, research assistance, coding support, debugging, and documentation. AI image generation was used to create the project logo.

Scientific and safety limitations

All demonstration astronaut profiles and health readings are synthetic. The application does not connect to live NASA systems, spacecraft sensors, or real astronaut medical records. Gravity comparisons and early warning screening are experimental and are not clinically validated. The prototype is not a medical device, does not diagnose or recommend treatment, and does not replace qualified medical or mission procedures. Application level access controls have been demonstrated, but production grade database security has not been established.

Our mission: Healthy Astronauts , Successful Missions.
